long_biography.plain_text:
Engler's first Mexican-food venture, Los Primos, began in 1979 after he noticed a gap in the market. He and his brother expanded it across five states, then changed course when the concept struggled. After securing a financial partner, the brothers built a Taco Bell base that reached 13 restaurants.

A 1996 purchase of Minnesota's remaining 63 Taco Bell outlets transformed the business and created Border Foods. The brothers bought out their equity partner three years later, becoming owners and operators. Engler handled finance and strategy, eventually refocusing the group on Taco Bell after its experiments with other brands underperformed.
